description: "How NCodeGroup code encodes, decodes, parses and formats text, bytes, JSON, numbers, dates and URLs so that results are exact, independent of culture, and match the relevant specifications."

# Text and encoding

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Compute OIDC token hashes (such as `at_hash` and `c_hash`) over the value's ASCII octets. Verification must return false when the value or the claim is not ASCII, and computation must throw `ArgumentException` for a non-ASCII value.** OIDC Core §3.1.3.6 defines the hash over ASCII octets. Encoding the value as UTF-8 without a check quietly accepts input the specification does not allow. *Check:* Look for token-hash code that encodes the value with UTF-8 and never checks for ASCII, or that silently accepts non-ASCII input. <sub>Identity ADR-0273</sub>
- **Decode HTTP Basic credentials (RFC 7617) with standard padded Base64, never with Base64Url decode or length helpers.** RFC 7617 specifies standard Base64. Base64Url helpers compute the wrong sizes and decode some inputs incorrectly. *Check:* Look for Base64Url decode or length helpers used while parsing `Authorization: Basic` credentials. <sub>Identity ADR-0092</sub>
- **When you write a redirect URI into a `Location` header, percent-encode only the characters a header value cannot carry (non-ASCII, ASCII control characters and space). Leave the rest of the string as written, including any fragment such as `#_=_`.** The client must receive the response at exactly the redirect URI it registered or sent. Broader re-encoding changes the value. *Check:* Look for `Uri` or `UriBuilder` round-trips, or general URL encoding of the whole redirect URI, before `Location` is set. <sub>Identity ADR-0203</sub>
- **Count password length in Unicode code points (runes, for example with `EnumerateRunes()`) over the whole password, never in UTF-16 `char`s, and never truncate the password.** NIST SP 800-63B-4 counts each code point as one character, so a surrogate pair is one character, and the whole password must be judged. *Check:* Flag password length checks that use `.Length` on a string or char span, and any truncation or substring of a password before it is validated, hashed or compared. <sub>Identity ADR-0236</sub>
- **When you normalize a password with `string.Normalize`, catch the `ArgumentException` it throws for invalid UTF-16 (such as an unpaired surrogate) and use the password as provided. Handle this the same way on the hash path and the verify path.** A string with an unpaired surrogate has no NFC form. Hashing and verification still have to treat it the same way every time, or a valid password stops verifying. *Check:* Look for `string.Normalize` calls on password input that do not handle `ArgumentException`, or that handle it differently on the hash and verify paths. <sub>Identity ADR-0243</sub>
- **Parse a typed claim value strictly in its declared XML Schema type's lexical space with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. Use `NumberStyles.Integer` for integer types and `NumberStyles.Float` for real types, never `NumberStyles.Any`, `Number` or `Currency`, and never the current culture.** Lenient parsing accepts thousands separators, currency symbols and negatives in parentheses, so a value such as "1,000" typed as integer64 silently becomes 1000. *Check:* Look for `int`/`long`/`uint`/`ulong`/`double.TryParse` calls on claim values that pass a lenient `NumberStyles` or do not pass `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. <sub>Identity ADR-0122</sub>
- **Give a typed `Claim` its value in the declared type's XML Schema lexical form, and format numbers with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`.** A culture-formatted value such as "1,000" does not parse strictly as its declared type, so it is emitted as a string instead of a number. *Check:* Look for `new Claim(...)` calls with a numeric `ClaimValueTypes` whose value comes from `ToString()` without `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` or from a format string that depends on culture. <sub>Identity ADR-0122; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **To test whether a JSON number is a whole value, use `decimal` (`TryGetDecimal` and compare with `decimal.Truncate`), not `double`.** Binary rounding in `double` turns `60.0000000000000001` into 60 and accepts it. `decimal` represents it exactly and rejects it. *Check:* Look for `TryGetDouble`, `GetDouble` or `double` arithmetic used to decide whether a JSON number is an integer. <sub>Identity ADR-0277</sub>
- **Parse date/time strings with `NCode.Json.DateCoercion.TryParseDateTimeOffset` or `TryParseDateTime`, never with a direct `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` `Parse` or `TryParse` call. Parse only values that are declared to be dates, and never use date parsing to guess whether an arbitrary string is a date.** All packages share one invariant-culture date policy, and hand-written parsing drifts away from it. Guessing from untyped strings would turn values such as "1.2" or "10:30" into dates. *Check:* Look for `DateTime.Parse`/`TryParse` or `DateTimeOffset.Parse`/`TryParse` on date strings in production code, and for date parsing applied to untyped string values. <sub>Identity ADR-0121; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Encode identifiers placed in a URL path segment with `encodeURIComponent` and decode them with `decodeURIComponent`. Treat a blank value or a malformed encoding as no match instead of throwing or passing it through.** Encoding the identifier as a single segment lets any name survive the round trip. Rejecting blank or malformed input keeps it from resolving to an unintended route. *Check:* Look for paths built by concatenating raw identifiers, and for `decodeURIComponent` calls without a try/catch or without a blank-value check. <sub>Identity ADR-0174</sub>
- **Pass `contentEncoding: SecureEncoding.UTF8` (from `NCode.Buffers`) explicitly on every `TypedResults.Text` and `TypedResults.Content` call. For a media type that has no charset parameter (such as `application/jwt`), write strict UTF-8 bytes yourself instead of passing an encoding.** Analyzers cannot tell whether an encoding was passed, so review has to enforce it. Explicit strict UTF-8 keeps responses correct and correctly labeled, and charset-less media types must not get a charset added. *Check:* Look for `TypedResults.Text` or `TypedResults.Content` calls that omit `contentEncoding` or pass a non-strict encoding such as `Encoding.UTF8`, and for charset-less media types that end up with a charset. <sub>Identity ADR-0266</sub>
- **Write HTML response bodies with `HttpResponse.WriteAsync(text, SecureEncoding.UTF8, cancellationToken)` from `NCode.Buffers`.** This reuses the shared strict-UTF-8 writing stack instead of ad-hoc encoders. *Check:* Look for HTML bodies written with `Encoding.UTF8`, encoded by hand into byte arrays, or written through other ad-hoc writers. <sub>Identity ADR-0114</sub>
- **Read and default `JsonElement` values with the shared `NCode.Json` helpers (`TryGetPropertyValue<T>`, `TryGetValue<T>`, `IsNullOrUndefined()`, `JsonElements.EmptyObject`/`OrEmptyObject()`). Do not write `TryGetProperty` + `ValueKind` + `GetString()`/`GetInt64()` chains, local copies of these helpers, or re-parse `"{}"`.** The shared helpers convert by `ValueKind` and never throw, while the bare getters throw when the kind does not match. They live in a dependency-free package so every layer can use them. *Check:* Look for manual `TryGetProperty`/`ValueKind`/`Get*` chains, `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null` or `Undefined` checks, hand-built empty-object elements, and parsing of "{}". <sub>Identity ADR-0055; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Parse JSON text with `JsonElement.Parse` instead of `JsonDocument.Parse` in new production and test code, and especially instead of `JsonDocument.Parse(...).RootElement.Clone()`.** `JsonElement.Parse` returns a detached value with no document to own and dispose, and it is the standard API going forward. *Check:* Look for newly added `JsonDocument.Parse` calls, or other `JsonDocument` usage, where `JsonElement.Parse` would work. <sub>Identity ADR-0056; Identity review of #382</sub>
- **Format non-string values embedded in validation, problem or diagnostic messages with the invariant culture, for example with `string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...)` or `IFormattable.ToString(null, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`.** Messages name values such as `TimeSpan`s, numbers and dates, and they have to read the same whatever culture the server runs in. *Check:* Look for string interpolation, `ToString()` or `string.Format` without an `IFormatProvider` that puts non-string values into validation or problem messages. <sub>Identity ADR-0240</sub>
- **Create a `string` only for a non-secret value at a storage or wire boundary (such as an envelope in a text column, a wrapped key or a KMS encryption context), and build it once, in place, with `string.Create`.** Building the string in place avoids intermediate allocations. Limiting strings to boundaries keeps secret material out of immutable managed strings that cannot be wiped. *Check:* Flag concatenation, `StringBuilder` or intermediate `ToString` calls used to build encoded envelope or key text, and any string that holds secret material. <sub>Identity ADR-0235</sub>
- **Write constant bytes that are valid UTF-8 text as `u8` literals (`ReadOnlySpan<byte>`), not with `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("...")` or hand-written byte arrays. Keep explicit byte arrays only for invalid UTF-8 or error-condition tests.** `u8` literals are compile-time constants that do not allocate and are less error-prone than encoding at runtime or spelling out bytes. *Check:* Look for `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("literal")` stored in a field or computed per call, and for hand-written byte arrays that spell valid UTF-8 text. <sub>Identity ADR-0116; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In tests, write strings that are not NFC or are otherwise sensitive to normalization with Unicode escapes (for example `"café"`), never as pasted characters.** An editor can normalize pasted characters and silently change the test input. *Check:* Look for normalization tests whose string literals contain combining or composed characters directly instead of escapes. <sub>Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md</sub>
- **Remove the UTF-8 BOM from generated EF Core migration files, and revert any model snapshot whose only change is a BOM.** Repository files are BOM-less, but `dotnet ef migrations add` writes BOMs and re-saves the snapshot even when nothing changed. *Check:* Look for new migration files that start with a BOM, and snapshot diffs whose only change is the BOM. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Save text files as UTF-8 without a BOM and with LF line endings.** This is the shared encoding convention (`charset = utf-8` in `.editorconfig`). BOMs and CRLF cause noisy diffs. *Check:* Flag changed files that start with a UTF-8 BOM or contain CRLF line endings. <sub>Identity project-template.instructions.md</sub>
